instantiated_cells.justification: Principals must file expense statements on or before July 31 and January 31, indicating semiannual rather than annual reporting.
The statute specifies twice-yearly filing dates (July 31 and January 31), not monthly reports.
The law provides a fixed twice-yearly schedule and does not create an alternative 'other' periodic reporting frequency for principals' expense statements.
Required filings are due on July 31 and January 31 for each reporting period, which is not quarterly reporting.
Expense statements are due July 31 and January 31 and cover the preceding 6-month 'reporting period,' i.e., semiannual reporting.
Reporting periods are defined as fixed 6-month intervals, not three times per year tied to the legislative calendar.
The registration statement requires a description of the business activity or nature/purposes of the principal, disclosing the nature of the business/organization.
The expense statement must include lobbying expenditures and obligations including "compensation to lobbyists for lobbying" and reimbursements.
The required time record itemizes time spent meeting with officials but does not require naming specific contacts or listing each contact made.
Principals must report each legislative proposal/budget bill subject/proposed rule number or, if none, each topic of lobbying communications and proportion of time by topic.

The expense statement must list the name, date, and amount of any reimbursement provided to specified officials under § 13.621(7)(a), which can include expense items such as travel/lodging/meal costs.

The statute requires reporting of non-compensation lobbying costs such as preparation, research/analysis, certain paid advertising to urge public influence, and office overhead/utilities/supplies when applicable.
When payments to any lobbyist exceed $200 in a reporting period, the principal must list the lobbyist's "name and address" and the total amount paid/incurred.

The expense statement requires listing each lobbyist (by name and address) for whom lobbying expenditures/obligations exceed $200 during the reporting period, which in practice can require naming all lobbyists above that threshold.
Neither the registration nor the expense statement provisions require disclosure of the principal's major financial contributors.
A principal's registration statement must specify the principal’s name and business address.

Principals must report each "legislative proposal" (bill/resolution), budget bill subject, and proposed administrative rule number in connection with which they made or intend to make a lobbying communication.
Principals must report the aggregate total amount of lobbying expenditures made and obligations incurred for lobbying by the principal and all lobbyists for the principal (with specified exclusions).
The expense statement must include compensation to lobbyists and, above $200 per lobbyist per reporting period, list each lobbyist and the total amount paid/incurred to that lobbyist.
The statute requires a daily itemization of time spent lobbying and, for lobbyists paid over $200, an itemized listing by lobbyist of the total amounts paid.
Associations must report the approximate number of members and CEO name, but there is no requirement to list all sponsors or members.
The principal’s expense statement must list the name (and address) of each lobbyist for whom the principal’s lobbying expenditures/obligations exceed $200 during the reporting period.
